# Synthetic sample STDF files

**Every file here is synthetic: generated by `stdf-cypher synthetic-sample`, not recorded on a tester.**
No value comes from a real product, lot or test floor.
The file names start with `synthetic_`, the lot IDs with `SYNTH_`, the tester is `SYNTH TESTER01`, and MIR EXEC_TYP is `stdf-cypher-synthetic-sample`, so a file stays recognisable outside this folder.

Use them to try stdf-cypher and to compare its results with other STDF tools.
The files are plain, little-endian STDF V4.

## Two record profiles

The same data is written twice:

| Folder | Profile |
|---|---|
| `plain/` | The records stdf-cypher's own tests use: summary TSR, HBR per site and in total, SBR in total, PCR per site, PMR with MPR, units as the tester shows them (uA, mV) |
| `tc_profile/` | The custom test-cell (TC) STDF profile: see below |

The values are the same draws in both: a TC-profile file logs IDD as `A` with RES_SCAL 6 where the plain file logs `uA`.
stdf-cypher gives the same Qualification drift results on both sets.

### What the TC profile adds

* PCR, HBR, SBR and TSR for every site and as a summary (HEAD_NUM and SITE_NUM 255); TSR for every test, PTR, MPR and FTR, with execution, fail and alarm counts and the min, max, sum and sum of squares of the logged results.
* PGR and PLR beside PMR, because the files use MPR.
* Base units only (`A`, `V`, `Hz`, `s`), with the scale in RES_SCAL.
* Part text as `name_value` elements separated by `;`: `LOT_SYNTH_A;WAFER_01;X_3;Y_-2` for wafer sort, `LOT_SYNTH_LOOP;2DID_SYNTH_LOOP-DUT001` for final test.
* MIR filled for genealogy: CMOD_COD `T` for a first run (`R` for a 100% retest), FLOW_ID, facility, floor, operator, family, package, spec, setup and serial fields, and USER_TXT saying the data is synthetic.
* SDR with the handler or prober, probe card, loadboard, DIB and socket IDs.
* GDR.MIR_ADD and GDR.AUTOMATION, and GDR.REF_DIE after each WIR in wafer sort.
* One soft and one hard bin per test number, with a name for every bin.

The GDR field layout is an assumption: the profile summary used here names these GDRs and what they carry, not their fields.
Each is written as its name (`C*n`) followed by `KEY=value` text fields, for example `REF_DIE`, `X_DIST=0`, `Y_DIST=0`, `X=0`, `Y=0`.
Check them against the full profile document before relying on them.

Not generated: ATR (no post-processing), RDR (no offline retest of selected bins), the high-parallelism site encoding (more than 255 sites), the V4-2007.1 scan-diagnosis records, the R&R and PAT/SPL file types (MIR PROC_ID `RR` and `PAT`), and the profile's lowercase file-name layouts.

## demo

Wafer sort, 3 wafers, 4 sites, 40 tests, 1,443 parts per file.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `synthetic_demo_lotA.stdf` | Lot SYNTH_A, the reference lot |
| `synthetic_demo_lotB_shifted.stdf` | Lot SYNTH_B: other parts, every test mean shifted by 0.6 sigma |
| `synthetic_demo_lotA_tester2.stdf` | Lot SYNTH_A's parts again on a second tester: re-measurement noise of 0.3 sigma and an offset of 1.5 sigma on every 3rd test |

Use them for Compare (lot A against lot B), Correlation and Match (lot A against its second-tester run), ANOVA and Wafer maps.

## qual

Final test touchdown files for the Qualification drift reports: 4 sites, the same unit on each site in every touchdown (a loop), 2 parametric tests (VDD and IDD).
Site 3 yields less than the other sites in every file.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `synthetic_endurance_4site_1200loops.stdf` | Endurance trial: 1,200 loops on each site |
| `synthetic_loop_old_tp.stdf` | 25x loop compare, old test program: 40 loops |
| `synthetic_loop_new_tp.stdf` | 25x loop compare, new test program: 40 loops, about 5% of the site slots left empty |

What stdf-cypher reports on them with the default settings:

* Endurance check with `--max-loops 1000`: sites 1, 2 and 4 are compared; site 3 is dropped because its yield is below 95%.
* 25x loop compare: sites 1, 2 and 4 are compared; site 3 is dropped because it has fewer than 25 good loops in each file.

## Making them again

The same command writes the same bytes.
For the `tc_profile` set, add `--profile tc` and write to `tc_profile/` instead of `plain/`.

```
stdf-cypher synthetic-sample plain/demo/synthetic_demo_lotA.stdf --lot SYNTH_A
stdf-cypher synthetic-sample plain/demo/synthetic_demo_lotB_shifted.stdf --lot SYNTH_B --seed 2 --shift 0.6
stdf-cypher synthetic-sample plain/demo/synthetic_demo_lotA_tester2.stdf --lot SYNTH_A --meas-noise 0.3 --tester-offset 1.5
stdf-cypher synthetic-sample plain/qual/synthetic_endurance_4site_1200loops.stdf --lot SYNTH_LOOP --touchdowns 1200 --sites 4 --dut-pool 4 --empty 0 --seed 3
stdf-cypher synthetic-sample plain/qual/synthetic_loop_old_tp.stdf --lot SYNTH_LOOP --touchdowns 40 --sites 4 --dut-pool 4 --empty 0 --seed 3
stdf-cypher synthetic-sample plain/qual/synthetic_loop_new_tp.stdf --lot SYNTH_LOOP --touchdowns 40 --sites 4 --dut-pool 4 --empty 0.05 --seed 4
```
